subject: Rate stitch & commit reshaping for renewal
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Owen Martinez <owen.martinez@helix-commerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Rate stitch & commit reshaping for renewal

Owen —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, Helix's forecasting shows a ~2-3x step-up in inference volume starting in Q1 once the recommendation rollout finishes. To keep the unit economics predictable for you and preserve runway on capacity, we've sketched a renewal posture that blends a committed uplift with an initial price-hold window. High-level proposal attached (pricing_v3.xlsx).

Summary:
- Term: 12 months (option to extend to 24 months for additional concession)
- Commit: 3x current committed tokens (monthly true-up available)
- Price: 20% discount on committed unit rate for the term
- Price-hold: fixed rate for the first 90 days after renewal effective date (protects your Q1 launch)
- Credits: 10% of any monthly overage applied as account credit if monthly usage exceeds 120% of committed baseline

If Helix can commit to an earlier PO (targeting 11/30), we can:
- Add a $25k migration/onboarding credit applied to month 1 invoice
- Offer a one-time invoice deferral option to align with your procurement cadence

Open questions I flagged for ops: monthly vs. annual true-up, whether the 90-day hold can be measured from go-live vs. contract effective date, and whether you need a separate SLA clause for the burst window. Priyom — please review the attached for the runtime/ops constraints and confirm feasible burst ceilings for the 3x commit.

Next steps: if this looks directionally right, I can circulate a redlineable term sheet and route to Legal/Finance for a 7-day turnaround.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0139
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_v3.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet with rate ladder and example P&L)
From: Owen Martinez <owen.martinez@helix-commerce.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helix-commerce.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:48:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Rate stitch & commit reshaping for renewal

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear summary. This is directionally helpful. A couple of clarifying items from procurement and our finance team: 

1) True-up cadence: Procurement prefers monthly true-up rather than annual so we can avoid a large true-up invoice after a growth quarter. Is Redwood able to support monthly true-ups with automated metering? If so, what's the minimum reporting latency?

2) Multi-year ask: If we extend to 24 months, what's the deepest you can go on committed unit discount? Our CFO is asking whether an extra 2-3% is realistic for a 24-month signature.

3) Price-hold measurement: Can the 90-day price-hold be tied to go-live (post-feature rollout) vs. effective date? That would protect customer-facing launch volatility.

We attached our procurement timeline and required PO template for your team to preview. If you can get a term-sheet to us by EOD Tuesday we can loop Legal.

Thanks —
Owen Martinez
Head of Platform Ops, Helix Commerce
owen.martinez@helix-commerce.com | +1 212-555-0462

Attachments: procurement_timeline.pdf (Helix procurement schedule + PO template)

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rate stitch & commit reshaping for renewal

Owen —

Quick follow with answers and an alternate concession set if Helix is willing to extend to 24 months. See draft term sheet attached (term-sheet-draft.pdf). Key clarifications: 

- Monthly true-up: yes — we can support monthly metering and settlement. Reporting latency is 48 hours; billing runs on the first business day of the following month. We can provide weekly consumption snapshots during ramp.

- 24-month concession: we can move to an 18% committed unit rate (vs 20% for 12 months) + an additional one-time onboarding credit of $25k applied to month 1. We are willing to hold the Q1 price for 120 days if Helix signs by 11/30.

- Price-hold anchor: we can anchor the 120-day hold to go-live (defined as when the primary production endpoint receives traffic flagged as "launch" in your release manifest). Ops/SE will need a short acceptance test window to validate the routing and KV-cache priming before the hold begins. Priyom — please confirm ops acceptance criteria.

If that structure is acceptable, I'll route this to Legal to issue an amendment (DocuSign link below) and to Finance to confirm invoice timing. Please note the monthly true-up means we'll run small statement-of-account emails each month and apply credits to the next invoice cycle.

DocuSign (preview): https://www.docusign.com/en/view/abc123-amendment
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

Can you confirm procurement's required billing contact and whether Helix prefers Net30 or Net45? If you can get me a tentative PO date (your PDF shows a mid-December approval), we'll align the amendment effective date accordingly.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Rate stitch & commit reshaping for renewal

Team —

Copying key asks and recommended internal moves before we hand to Sales Ops/Finance/Legal:

- Offer summary for Helix (internal): 12mo @ 20% or 24mo @ 18% + $25k onboarding credit; 120-day price-hold anchored to go-live; monthly true-up with 48hr reporting latency; 10% monthly overage credit guard above 120% baseline.

- Ask Sales Ops: reserve burst capacity for Helix at current rate card ceilings during the 120-day hold and add migration credit to month 1 invoice. Work with Priyom to set burst ceilings and KPIs for automatic fallback.

- Ask Finance: prepare Net30 and Net45 invoice templates and confirm whether the $25k onboarding credit must be invoiced as a negative line item or applied as post-invoice credit.

- Ask Legal: prep amendment and confirm no SLA exposure beyond standard SLOs; flag any procurement redlines (PO vs. signed amendment).

I suggest we mark deal in HubSpot HLX-2026-RNW-47 and set close-probability to 75% pending PO. If Procurement pushes for another 1-2% discount, consider offering a one-time $25k migration credit instead of deeper percentage concession.

I'll follow-up with Sales Ops to create the internal checklist.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
